model: SISGEO digital instruments, RS-485 Modbus (firmware 3.x normal mode)
applies_to: SISGEO digital instruments with firmware 0x0300 or later running in normal (non-legacy) mode, protocol manual EN 05/20.
summary: Common Modbus RTU register set of SISGEO's digital geotechnical instruments (in-place inclinometers, tiltmeters, piezometers, extensometers). Input registers give update counters, physical readings as IEEE-754 floats and fixed-point integers, electrical readings, supply voltage and internal temperature/humidity; holding registers hold version, address, baud rate, timed-mode options and power-down.

addressing.note: Registers are printed as hexadecimal addresses. The manual lists a holding register at 0x0000 (HR_VERSION_FW, 'read Holding Register 0x0000'), which only exists in 0-based protocol addressing, so the printed hex values are the wire addresses. The input-register tables print short forms such as 0x202; 'documented' keeps the form used in each table.

notes: Word order: the manual shows the float's sign/exponent bits in the first register (e.g. 0x202) and the rest in the second, and states for integer and fixed-point pairs that the most significant word comes first. All listed 32-bit values are ABCD.
The channel-configuration 'Scale' pair is the exception: the manual says it is stored least significant word first. Those configuration registers (0x0148 onward) are not listed.
What each physical channel holds (tilt, pressure, temperature, etc.) depends on the instrument; see its own datasheet and user manual.
Only physical channels 0-14 (float), fixed-point channels 0-7 and electrical channels 0-7 are listed; fixed-point and electrical blocks run to channel 14 at the same 2-register spacing.

Raw ADC registers (0x260+) are left out: the manual's table repeats addresses 0x260-0x26E for channels 7-14, so the layout cannot be trusted. Legacy-mode registers (0x0100-0x012B input) are also left out.
IR_PHYSICAL_COUNT changes when a new averaged reading is ready; the manual advises waiting for two increments of IR_PHYSICAL_CHANGE after an input change before trusting the value.
IR_TEMPERATURE is listed as signed (INT16); the manual gives it in tenths of a degree Celsius but does not state the sign convention.

integration.summary: Read IR_PHYSICAL_COUNT plus the physical float channels in one FC04 request from 0x0200, decode the floats high word first, and use the count to detect new readings.
integration.enable: Instruments ship in always-on mode (except DEX/DEX-S) at address and baud set in the user configuration; no enable step.
quirks: Input and holding registers share address numbers but are different data; use FC04 for readings and FC03 for configuration.
Floats and 32-bit integers are high word first; the configuration Scale pair is low word first.
setup: 9600 baud, 8N1 by default; baud stored in 0x0142 as baud/100.
In timed mode units come online after initial + address x incremental delay seconds.
gotchas: Writing 0xFF to HR_RESET switches the unit off until power is cycled.
The moving average needs about two IR_PHYSICAL_CHANGE increments to settle after the input changes.

verified.method: independent re-check of every register against the source PDF
